title: POC scoping - benchmark harness integration
summary: Redwood and Vertex Retail scoped the POC benchmark plan: integrate Vertex's inference scripts into Redwood's benchmark harness, agree on workload sizing (RPS, seq len distribution), decide streaming vs non-streaming modes to test, and confirm timeline for runs and deliverables. Action items: share scripts and sample data, Redwood to provide harness integration guide and run baseline tests, schedule benchmark execution window next week.
topics: benchmark metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per token)
next_steps: Vertex: share canonical inference scripts + sample dataset by 2026-03-26
Redwood: provision test tenant and repo access, share harness integration guide by 2026-03-27
Redwood: deliver baseline report within 3 business days after runs
action_items: Ethan Moore: provide customer scripts, data samples, and expected RPS distribution by 2026-03-26
Aisha Patel: send pricing/commitment options and POC SOW draft by 2026-03-26
Marco Ruiz: integrate scripts into Redwood harness and run initial smoke tests by 2026-03-27

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-24 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood SE), Ethan (Vertex Head of ML), Sara (Platform), James (PM), Priya (SRE)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): okay everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, agenda is to nail down the benchmark plan and how we integrate your scripts into our harness
00:22 Speaker 2 (Ethan): great, thanks aisha. quick context: our primary goal for the poc is to prove cost and latency at production loads for our recommendation stream. success metric is p95 < 300ms for 512 tokens and cost per 1k requests under $X (we'll fill numbers), and functional parity with our current model outputs
00:45 Speaker 3 (Marco): got it. couple clarifying q's: is the request pattern mostly streaming responses or single-shot generation? and do you have variable seq lengths?
00:58 Speaker 2 (Ethan): mainly streaming for recommendations; some batch scoring for nightly re-ranks. seq lengths skew short 64-128 for most requests but we have a tail up to 1024 for some internal workflows
01:20 Speaker 4 (Sara): also we do a hybrid where the UI requests an initial chunk then we stream additional tokens as user scrolls, so streaming latency is critical for perceived performance
01:40 Speaker 3 (Marco): ok that means we should test both streaming and non-streaming modes. our harness supports simulated streaming (chunked responses) and raw non-streamed endpoints. we'll want to run separate experiments: (A) streaming steady-state latency per-chunk, (B) end-to-end p95 for non-streaming full response, and (C) throughput stress tests for peak RPS
02:05 Speaker 5 (James): timeline question — how long to get a meaningful baseline?
02:12 Speaker 1 (Aisha): if you can share scripts and sample data this week, marco can integrate and run smoke tests in 24-48 hours, then full runs typically take 1-2 days depending on permutations; we'll then produce the baseline report within 72 hours after runs
02:30 Speaker 2 (Ethan): sounds reasonable. on sizing — we see steady 150 RPS average on peak, bursts to 400 RPS during promotions. want to test at 1x, 2x, 3x those numbers
02:50 Speaker 3 (Marco): noted. we'll parameterize the harness to run at 150/300/450 RPS with traffic shaping, and also vary concurrency and batch sizes. can you confirm average tokens per response and kv cache hit expectations?
03:08 Speaker 2 (Ethan): avg tokens ~80, but tokenization differences might change that a little, we'll include tokenizer script. kv cache hits are high for session-based users, maybe 60-70% hit rate
03:28 Speaker 6 (Priya): security question — for private tenant runs we'll need to ensure logs don't contain PII and the harness can point to our staging VPC. Do you support VPC peering or connector?
03:44 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes we have options: hosted harness runs can be done in Redwood's environment with redaction, or we can run the harness connectors in your VPC. for POC we usually do staging peered access or provide an on-prem runner if needed. we documented options in the SSO/KMS paper but we'll follow your requirements
04:10 Speaker 1 (Aisha): i'll note action items for who provides what — ethan you'll share scripts, sara will check access modality, we will provide the harness integration guide and initial branch to drop scripts into
04:30 Speaker 2 (Ethan): one more thing, how do you measure cost? we need clarity — token-level cost, compute minutes, and also amortized infra?
04:44 Speaker 3 (Marco): we compute cost per 1k requests using the actual tokens consumed plus GPU runtime and include misc overheads. for apples-to-apples we'll run the same prompt set on your current infra and on Redwood to report delta. bring your cost model or we can approximate
05:05 Speaker 4 (Lina): technical detail: for streaming tests we simulate chunked send with N tokens per chunk, and measure per-chunk latency and cumulative time to first meaningful payload. we also measure memory/KV cache pressure during long sessions
05:35 Speaker 5 (James): regarding scripts — our current inference pipeline wraps model calls behind a small adapter. can you support python scripts + dockerized runners?
05:48 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, the harness accepts multiple runners: direct python adapter, dockerized entrypoint, or a GRPC shim. easiest is to provide a small python adapter with a standard interface we show in the guide
06:10 Speaker 2 (Ethan): ok we'll prepare that. what about model variants — we'll want tests on our quantized 4-bit and also unquantized baseline, and maybe an LLM alternative for fallback
06:26 Speaker 3 (Marco): we can run multiple model variants; note that quantized runs have different latency/cost tradeoffs and slightly different output distributions. we'll surface quality deltas in the report (ROUGE/BLEU-ish or custom evals you provide)
06:46 Speaker 1 (Aisha): can we talk about success criteria to declare POC a win? Ethan?
06:52 Speaker 2 (Ethan): p95 latency under 300ms for 512 tokens in streaming for 150 RPS steady, scaling to 450 RPS with graceful degradation but not catastrophic failures. cost per 1k requests under our target (we'll confirm number). Also no functional regressions beyond agreed thresholds on our eval prompts
07:15 Speaker 5 (James): and timeline wise if we start integration by Friday we can get results by next week which fits our exec review cycle
07:25 Speaker 1 (Aisha): perfect. Marco i'll hand off the integration work and we'll aim for the smoke tests by 2026-03-27
07:33 Speaker 3 (Marco): quick technical note — to simulate your kv cache hit pattern we'll add a synthetic session id distribution; if you have real session traces that would be ideal, otherwise we'll use the patterns you described
07:50 Speaker 6 (Priya): for compliance, we need SOC2 and audit logs access for the benchmark runs; will you provide obfuscated logs and an audit trail?
08:02 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, we can provide audit logs and redact PII. for private deployments we can enable customer-managed KMS and retain logs per your retention policy. we'll include the SOC2/ISO packet in the docs we share
08:25 Speaker 4 (Lina): i'll attach the harness doc link in chat and the example adapter. it's light — basically a predict(input) -> response interface
08:40 Speaker 2 (Ethan): sounds good. one last thing: for streaming we need to ensure early token emission (we don't want large head-of-line blocking), how do you handle batching in streaming mode?
09:00 Speaker 3 (Marco): we do adaptive batching that respects streaming SLOs — low-latency requests go through fast-path without being batched into large groups; the harness can toggle batch size thresholds and max batch windows. we'll capture per-path metrics in the report
09:24 Speaker 1 (Aisha): ok recap: Vertex will share scripts, datasets, session traces; Redwood provides harness guide, integrates scripts, runs smoke, then full runs; deliver baseline report within 72h of runs. dates recapped in next steps.
09:45 Speaker 2 (Ethan): can you also include the raw logs and a sample dashboard so we can hook it into our back-of-the-envelope cost model?
09:52 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes we'll include CSV exports and a dashboard link; we'll also share the raw token counts per request and GPU runtime samples
10:05 Speaker 1 (Aisha): perfect. we'll follow up with SOW and SSO/access checklist. any other q's?
10:12 Speaker 5 (James): none from me
10:15 Speaker 6 (Priya): no 
10:17 Speaker 2 (Ethan): thanks all, appreciate the clear plan
10:20 Speaker 1 (Aisha): thanks everyone, talk soon

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (names sometimes mis-attributed and punctuation uneven). References to docs: harness guide link, SOW template, SOC2 packet.
notes: Transcript contains candid scoping about streaming vs non-streaming, kv cache simulation, and cost metrics. Customer emphasized session-based cache hits and burst traffic patterns. Redwood to run tests at 150/300/450 RPS and report back.
